answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and expiring contract create pressure to switch to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2), but the assembly line has no buffer (94% of committed volume) and switching vendors introduces onboarding and delivery-risk uncertainty that directly conflicts with the primary objective of not increasing delivery risk. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating with the incumbent using market benchmarking can recover real margin and improve terms without disrupting the stable, proven integration noted in memory_c1. Given only one decision slot and a hard 14-day deadline, negotiating with the incumbent is the lower-risk path that can partially address the cost mandate while preserving delivery continuity; switching primary vendor is deferred until its historical claims can be verified against current capacity constraints. I chose to verify memory_c2 because it is the strongest lever toward the risky action (full vendor switch) and its original context (buffer levels, volume assumptions) is critical to know before treating it as applicable now.
